axis_log: SIDE-DECOMPOSITION (the lane's mandated first step) - VERDICT: the multiset headline is NOT a decoy here, it is exactly the carrier set. Four clusters: (1) ours-only li @0x50 and (2) target-only li @0x54 form a COUNT-NEUTRAL entry reorder pair that cancels; (3) ours-only fmr @0x998 and (4) ours-only fmr @0xf5c are each +1 on OUR side. After the neutral pair cancels, the entire delta is the two fmr. CORRECTION TO THE WORK CLAIM: the claim briefed move_logic10 as '2 SHORT'. It is 2 LONG - target 1085, ours 1087, ours-only -2 fmr, a SURPLUS. Live probe confirms T1085/O1087. Any future pass must delete two instructions, never add two.

AXIS 1 (NEGATIVE, reverted): rewrite blocks B (enemy.c:3320) and C (:3522) into block A's explicit 3-arm form with a third `else av = cand;` arm. Motivation was sound and NEW: the predecessor record inferred 'target's block B is the 2-arm shape' from the absence of a third else-branch, but a 3-arm form whose else arm is register-coalesced emits ZERO instructions and is byte-indistinguishable, so that inference was unsound. Measured: real 476->474 but insns O1087->O1089 and multiset 2t->4t (ours-only -2 b -2 fmr). MWCC materialized the else arm as a real `b`+`fmr` pair rather than coalescing. Count parity outranks real; reverted.

AXIS 2 (NEGATIVE on the arbitrating metric, reverted): drop the f64 temp entirely and normalize in place - `if (cand > PI) cand = cand - 2PI; else if (cand <= -PI) cand = 2PI + cand;`. Measured real 476->458 (an 18-line gain) at IDENTICAL count (1087) and IDENTICAL multiset size (2t), residual respelled from ours-only -2 fmr to ours-only -2 frsp. It was banked as best and gated GREEN (66 siblings, GATE OK, full ninja main.dol OK) - and then REJECTED on fuzzy: 98.8940% -> 98.4470%, a 0.45-point REGRESSION. Independent structural evidence agrees with fuzzy: target emits exactly ONE frsp, placed AFTER the if/else join at 0x9cc, which proves a f64 temp existed and was narrowed once; the no-temp form narrows per-arm and is the wrong shape. Reverted to the committed temp form and the gate baseline was restored.

AXIS 3 (NEUTRAL, axis dead, reverted): hoist `f64 av;` out of the inner blocks into the case-1 and default declaration lists next to `f32 cand;`, to change the FP web allocation rank while preserving the correct single-frsp-at-join shape. attributes.residual: Unchanged from baseline and now sharper: real 476, insns T1085/O1087, fuzzy 98.8940, frame 392 (MATCHES), slot map IDENTICAL (22/22). NAMED MECHANISM: regnorm classifies the function as a pure RENAMING bisimulation plus the 2 surplus fmr - every row regnorm marks STRUCTURAL is a branch-target displacement caused by the surplus itself (target 0x10d8 vs ours 0x10e0 = 8 bytes = 2 insns; 0xb1c vs 0xb20 = 4 bytes = 1 insn, i.e. after the first fmr). There is NO structural residual. At blocks B and C target coalesces cand_pre, the f64 temp and cand_post ALL into one callee-saved FPR (f28) and normalizes in place; ours coalesces cand_pre with cand_post (f30) but hands the f64 temp the volatile f1, so each block opens with a surplus `fmr f1,f30` and closes `frsp f30,f1`. DECISIVE NEW EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS NOT SOURCE-REACHABLE: block A of this SAME function (target 0x3bc-0x3fc) shows TARGET ITSELF declining the identical coalesce - it uses f1 for the temp and emits `fmr f1,f25` for its else arm - and OUR build reproduces target's block A instruction-for-instruction. So MWCC does it both ways inside one function with one source idiom; the discriminant is allocator-internal register pressure, not the source shape. WEBFRANK: still NOT eligible - a recolor rule cannot delete the two instructions, and coalescing them would leave `fmr fX,fX` no-ops, so counts would still differ. DO-NOT-RETRY: the f64-`cand` whole-function retype (already refuted in v2), the 3-arm/2-arm spelling swap in EITHER direction, the no-temp form, and the declaration-rank hoist.
